title: Arithmetic Operator Playground
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Enter two numbers and see all seven MicroPython arithmetic operators side by side, with a block picture that shows what integer division and remainder really mean.

educational.topic: MicroPython arithmetic operators and result types
learningObjectives: Predict the result of +, -, *, /, //, % and ** for two numbers
Predict whether each result is an int or a float
Explain integer division and remainder as full groups and leftovers
Choose the right operator for a robot task such as beeping every 5th loop
prerequisites: Integers and floats (Chapter 3: The Four Core Data Types)
Evaluating expressions in the REPL (Chapter 3: The REPL)

controls.label: Robot example
options: Split a speed of 30 in half: 30 / 2

simulationModel.modelType: Python 3 arithmetic evaluation with a grouping picture
equations: a % b = a - b * floor(a / b)
a / b always returns a float
assumptions: b is a whole number from 1 to 10, so division by zero cannot happen
Integer powers are computed exactly, like Python ints
limitations: Very long results are shortened in the table

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-check with a concrete grouping model
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Number inputs and presets driving a full results table and picture
keyQuestions: What do the green groups and orange leftovers stand for?
How can % make a robot beep on every 5th loop?
commonMisconceptions: Dividing two ints with / gives an int
// rounds to the nearest whole number instead of counting full groups
assessmentOpportunities: Prediction sheet for all seven operators
Exit ticket: write a % condition and compare 30 / 2 with 30 // 2
